I've finished the Q3 2025 analysis and saved it to `/work/answer.json`. Before computing Q3, I ran the same calculation on Q2, and it reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net revenue | `smb`, 289,375,597 KRW |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 249 |
| c. Category with the highest net revenue | `svc`, 251,013,953 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net revenue | `2025-08` |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | `u33@ex.com` |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 238 |
| g. Average net revenue per order | 684,190 KRW |
| h. Growth from August to September | −17.9% |

Three things about the data had to be handled before the Q2 check matched:

- **Time zone:** order timestamps are stored in UTC. The reference values only come out when the quarter boundaries are set in Korea time (UTC+9), so I used Korea time for both quarter and month boundaries.
- **Segment names:** the same segment is spelled inconsistently (e.g. `SMB`, `smb`, `Enterprise `), so I lowercased them and trimmed spaces before grouping.
- **Duplicate customers:** there are 300 customer rows but only 250 distinct emails. b and f matched the reference only when customers were counted by email, so I did the same for the refund totals in e.

**Check on a:** some duplicated customers have different segments on different rows. I used the segment of the row each order points to; that matched the Q2 reference, but this ambiguity remains.

STATUS: DONE
